newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu back in Kinshasa, resting -- aide.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu back in Kinshasa, resting -- aide.

text.p: Zaire's embattled President Mobutu Sese Seko returned to the capital Kinshasa on Monday following inconclusive weekend talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila, an aide said.

The veteran leader, who is battling cancer and a whirlwind rebellion, was resting at his presidential villa in Tshatshi military camp on the banks of the Zaire River, the aide told Reuters. Mobutu has not been seen in public since returning.
Kabila told a news conference at his Lubumbashi headquarters on Monday that his forces would chase Mobutu out of the capital Kinshasa if he did not hand over power by the time they arrived.
Mobutu, who has dominated Zaire since seizing power in 1965, offered at Sunday's talks on a South African ship in Congo's port of Pointe Noire to hand over to an elected president.
Kabila insisted his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire should be the transitional authority.
South African President Nelson Mandela, who hosted the meeting, said he would convene fresh talks between Mobutu and Kabila within eight to 10 days to "narrow the gap between the two parties".
Kabila said his forces were now less than 60 km (35 miles) from Kinshasa's Ndjili international airport, which is 25 km (16 miles) east of the capital.
Witnesses said Mobutu's plane landed there on Monday.

Emergency rule Prime Minister Likulia Bolongo met the plane but public access was restricted and although an impressive motorcade with smoked glass windows was seen leaving the airport no one actually saw the 66-year-old president.
